title: How many kilograms is each spice {{NAME_2}} buys?
description: {{NAME_2}} buys four spices in grams. Each weight is written over one thousand, made smaller, and read as thousandths to give a fraction and a decimal of a kilogram. Keeko doubts that twenty five grams is zero point two five kilograms.
teaching_notes: One idea: grams over one thousand gives kilograms, and the last digit of the decimal sits in the thousandths place. Watch for students who write twenty five grams as zero point two five kilograms.

source: {{NAME_2}} buys 50 g of cinnamon, 100 g of cumin seeds, 25 g of cardamom and 250 g of pepper at the market
video_script.why: The child knows decimals as tenths and hundredths and now needs thousandths to move between grams and kilograms.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four spice weights, each written over one thousand
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_2}} buys cinnamon, cumin seeds, cardamom and pepper at the market, each weighed in grams
video_script.wrong_answer: twenty five grams is zero point two five kilograms
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip writes twenty five grams as zero point two five kilograms. That is two hundred and fifty grams, ten times too much, because twenty five thousandths needs three places after the point.
video_script.payoff_line: Each spice now has its weight in kilograms.

final_answer.value: cinnamon 0.05 kg, cumin seeds 0.1 kg, cardamom 0.025 kg, pepper 0.25 kg
final_answer.spoken: zero point zero five, zero point one, zero point zero two five and zero point two five kilograms

maths_rules: 1 kg = 1000 g, so g over 1000 gives kg
the slip: 25 g written as 0.25 kg, but 0.25 kg = 250 g
video_script.design: One idea: grams over one thousand gives kilograms. Assumes tenths and hundredths. Wrong idea: twenty five grams is zero point two five kilograms. The four packets stay all video; the strip of one thousand parts stays through the ground; decimals appear only on the answer beat.

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>{{NAME_2}} buys four spices at the market.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>There are fifty grams of cinnamon and one hundred grams of cumin seeds. There are twenty five grams of cardamom and two hundred and fifty grams of pepper.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How can we write each weight in kilograms?

beats.on_screen: the packets and the question stay on the board while Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a strip for one kilogram is cut into 1000 equal parts, with one part shaded and labelled 1 g

marks.m1: the strip for one kilogram appears and is cut into one thousand parts
marks.m2: one part is shaded and the word thousandth is written beside it
marks.m3: the shaded part is labelled one gram

beats.colours: one part shaded in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A kilogram is made of one thousand grams, like a strip cut into one thousand equal parts.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One part out of a thousand equal parts is called a thousandth.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Every gram is one thousandth of a kilogram.

beats.on_screen: Given: cinnamon 50 g, cumin seeds 100 g, cardamom 25 g, pepper 250 g

marks.m1: the four weights are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, four weights in grams: fifty, one hundred, twenty five and two hundred and fifty.

beats.on_screen: To find: each weight in kg, as a fraction and as a decimal

marks.m1: the line To find is written under the weights

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to write each weight in kilograms, as a fraction and as a decimal.

marks.m1: the rule kilograms equal grams over one thousand is written
marks.m2: each weight is written over one thousand

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, write each weight over one thousand. We do this because one kilogram is one thousand grams.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty grams is fifty over one thousand of a kilogram, and the other weights go the same way.

marks.m1: the top and the bottom of each fraction are divided by the same number
marks.m2: the first two fractions become one over twenty and one over ten
marks.m3: the last two fractions become one over forty and one over four

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, divide the top and the bottom by the same number to make each fraction smaller.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty over one thousand becomes one over twenty. One hundred over one thousand is one over ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty five over one thousand is one over forty. Two hundred and fifty over one thousand is one over four.

beats.on_screen: place value table with tenths, hundredths, thousandths: 50 thousandths = 5 hundredths; 100 thousandths = 1 tenth; 25 thousandths = 2 hundredths and 5 thousandths; 250 thousandths = 2 tenths and 5 hundredths

marks.m1: the table with tenths, hundredths and thousandths appears
marks.m2: the first two weights fill their places
marks.m3: the last two weights fill their places

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, read each weight as thousandths in a place value table.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty thousandths is five hundredths. One hundred thousandths is one tenth.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty five thousandths is two hundredths and five thousandths. Two hundred and fifty thousandths is two tenths and five hundredths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: cinnamon 1/20 kg = 0.05 kg; cumin seeds 1/10 kg = 0.1 kg; cardamom 1/40 kg = 0.025 kg; pepper 1/4 kg = 0.25 kg

marks.m2: cinnamon and cumin seeds are written as fraction and decimal
marks.m3: cardamom and pepper are written as fraction and decimal

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Each spice now has its weight in kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Cinnamon is one over twenty, or zero point zero five, kilograms. Cumin seeds are one over ten, or zero point one, kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Cardamom is one over forty, or zero point zero two five, kilograms. Pepper is one over four, or zero point two five, kilograms.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the four packets
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 25 g = 0.25 kg; a packet of 250 g glows beside it; the bubble is struck through and 25/1000 = 0.025 appears

marks.m2: the packet of two hundred and fifty grams glows
marks.m3: the bubble is struck through and the right decimal is written

beats.colours: the doubt in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks twenty five grams is zero point two five kilograms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But zero point two five means twenty five hundredths of a kilogram. That is two hundred and fifty grams, the weight of the pepper.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty five thousandths needs three places after the point. The cardamom is zero point zero two five kilograms.
